Description: Sets the city's tax, policing, service, and infrastructure priorities for the year.
Outcome Details: The final budget passed with a 10.7% property-tax increase; the tax increase was the largest in more than a decade.

Description: Sets the city's tax rate, service levels, police funding, and capital priorities for 2025.
Outcome Details: The final budget passed with a 3.9% property-tax increase.

Description: Directs staff to prepare a 2026 budget with no property-tax increase.
Outcome Details: The final 2026 operating budget froze property taxes at 2025 levels.

Description: Calls for a $25-a-month transit pass for people earning less than $40,000.
Outcome Details: Council amended the motion to ask senior governments to create the pass, then approved it unanimously; Klassen and Meiszner were absent.

Description: Keeps the Empty Homes Tax at 3% rather than increasing it to 5%.
Outcome Details: Council approved the report-back motion without increasing the Empty Homes Tax to 5%; the higher rate would have generated an estimated $20 million annually for affordable housing.

Description: Direction to staff to accelerate climate measures, including supporting active transportation, EVs, heat pumps
Outcome Details: Set positive early signals but most action was most undone or paused by later ABC policy moves.

Vote: Allowing natural gas in new construction - Vote 1
Description: Suprise amendment directing staff to change by-law to allow natural gas for heating and hot water in new construction

Vote: Allowing natural gas in new construction - Vote 2
Description: After a huge public outcry

Vote: Allowing natural gas in new construction - Vote 3
Description: Natural gas lobby convinces Mayor Ken Sim to allow natural gas back in the guise of affordability.
Zero-means-zero budget with increases to the police budget and large cuts elsewhere.
Outcome Details: $8.3 million cut to energy retrofits program, and large reductions to staff working on sustainability work.

Description: Begins transferring parks and recreation governance from the elected Park Board to Council.
Outcome Details: Province didn't follow through with Ken Sim's request to abolish the Park Board.

Description: Directs staff to examine whether the city could use, hold, or accept Bitcoin.
Outcome Details: Luckily Vancouver never ended up investing in Bitcoin.

Description: Temporarily pauses new and ongoing Integrity Commissioner investigations while Council reviews the office's scope and mandate.
Outcome Details: Council later backed down and allowed the commissioner's work to resume in late 2024.

Description: Adopts direct structural safeguards protecting the Integrity Commissioner from political interference, including protections recommended by Reece Harding's independent review.
Outcome Details: The ABC majority used a strike-and-replace motion to direct staff to study the recommendations instead of immediately adopting structural firewalls.

Vote: Sanctioning Mayor Sim after Integrity Commissioner finding
Description: Deciding whether to sanction Mayor Ken Sim after an independent investigation found that he misused the influence of his office and harassed Councillor Sean Orr.
Outcome Details: Council imposed no sanctions and did not require an apology; the ABC majority questioned the investigation, while Mayor Sim was absent for a conflict of interest.

Description: Renter Office helped with tenant rights. Cost $600,000/year to run.
Outcome Details: The ABC majority voted to end the city's Renter Office with a last-minute amendment to a staff report that recommended it continue.

Vote: Grandview Highway and Southeast Marine social housing
Description: Approved two six-storey buildings providing 136 social-housing homes with supports.
Outcome Details: 136 social-housing units

Description: Directs staff to renew or extend temporary modular-housing leases, find longer-term sites, and avoid a net loss of supportive-housing units while permanent housing is built.
Outcome Details: The motion lost. The official minutes record the ABC councillors and Mayor Sim opposed, Pete Fry, Adriane Carr, and Christine Boyle in favour, and Rebecca Bligh absent.

Description: Incremental proposal from City planners to allow multiplexes in more neighbourhoods with only a small increase in density.
Outcome Details: Unanimous

Description: Considered a 17-storey, 170-home rental tower on a lower-density street under the Broadway Plan.
Outcome Details: 267 support and 144 opposition correspondence items

Vote: Right to Cool for strata buildings
Description: Giving tenants the right to install air conditioning
Outcome Details: Passed; Ken Sim and Lisa Dominato were absent.

Description: Approved three rental towers with more than 1,000 homes beside Commercial-Broadway Station, amid major affordability and scale concerns.
Outcome Details: Three towers; more than 1,000 rental homes. The final motion passed with Mike Klassen and Sean Orr opposed, Pete Fry abstaining, and Brian Montague absent.

Description: Replace site rezonings with citywide zoning for mixed-income social, supportive, and co-operative housing.
Outcome Details: Huge setback to the construction of new social housing in Vancouver.

Description: Changes zoning and related policies to accelerate SRO replacement, increase social housing, and create a $5 million Downtown Eastside Housing Revitalization Grant Program.
Outcome Details: Rebecca Bligh, Pete Fry, Sean Orr, and Lucy Maloney opposed after failing to pass amendments to protect existing SROs.

Description: Plan designed to transform 17 small commercial nodes across the city into walkable, mixed-use community hubs.
Outcome Details: Failed under NIMBY opposition; only minor ODP changes and space-efficient stair amendments were approved.

Description: Determines whether Vancouver seeks more speed and red-light cameras.
Outcome Details: Original motion replaced by amendment

Description: Adds funding for traffic-calming, crossings, medians, and safety upgrades.
Outcome Details: Added $3 million

Description: Allows VPD access to city traffic cameras, raising major privacy and surveillance questions.
Outcome Details: One councillor opposed

Description: Requires an updated road-safety strategy with clearer targets and accountability.
Outcome Details: Final motion passed unanimously; Mayor Ken Sim was absent.

Vote: Safe Streets for Trick or Treat
Description: Considers simpler, safer temporary street closures for Halloween block parties.
Outcome Details: Council referred the permit-streamlining and communications provisions to staff; Councillors Fry, Maloney, and Orr opposed, while Dominato was absent.

Description: Attempts to protect previously approved road-safety and active-transport projects from cuts.
Outcome Details: The amendment to preserve several road-safety and active-transport motions failed; the underlying staff-allocation report carried. Councillors Dominato, Kirby-Yung, Klassen, Meiszner, Montague, Zhou, and Mayor Sim opposed the amendment.

Vote: Vision Zero action-plan - lower speed limits downtown
Description: Would have lowered the speed limit to 30 or 40km/h on select major roadways with high pedestrian activity downtown
Outcome Details: Amended out of the plan by ABC.

Description: Approves a $2.1 million VPD budget increase and a one-time $11.2 million reallocation to address forecasted police-budget deficits.
Outcome Details: The final components passed with some councillors abstaining.

Description: Adds $2.64 million to the VPD budget, including ongoing and one-time funding for full implementation of body-worn cameras, plus related investigative and risk-management costs.
Outcome Details: Council approved the amendment as part of the 2025 budget.

Description: Directs the City not to enforce the indoor-smoking prohibition for Health Canada-approved supervised-consumption sites that meet WorkSafeBC requirements, enabling supervised inhalation services.
Outcome Details: Council adopted the resolution unanimously. It applied for two years and directed staff to evaluate the spaces and report back.

Vote: Blocking overdose prevention site in downtown Vancouver
Description: Directs staff to use all lawful city tools to prevent the opening of a proposed overdose prevention site at 900 Helmcken Street.
Outcome Details: Council approved the motion 7–6. All ABC councillors supported blocking the site; all opposition councillors opposed the motion.

Description: Rejects near-term protected active-transport lanes on Broadway while preserving an option to add them later.
Outcome Details: Council approved the interim Great Street design; the protected-lane option was deferred until after the Broadway Subway opens.

Description: Extends a reduced-speed pilot along Cornwall Avenue to protect people walking, cycling, and driving.
Outcome Details: Council amended the proposed 30 km/h limit to 40 km/h and carried the amended motion.

Description: Removes required minimum off-street parking in major west-side areas.
Outcome Details: Removed minimum general-purpose parking requirements for new developments in the West End and Broadway Plan areas; accessible, visitor, bicycle, and loading spaces remained required.

Description: Prioritizes rapid-transit planning along one of Vancouver's most congested corridors.
Outcome Details: Council endorsed advancing bus rapid transit and priority RapidBus projects, including the Hastings corridor.

Description: Tests a more pedestrian-oriented, car-free Water Street in Gastown.
Outcome Details: Council approved the July–August 2024 Gastown pedestrian-zone pilot; the amendment was defeated.

Description: Approves a crossing where pedestrians can move through the intersection in every direction.
Outcome Details: Council unanimously approved a Granville–Robson pedestrian-scramble pilot and requested a follow-up report.

Description: Supports restoring two-way vehicle traffic on Beach Avenue near Stanley Park.
Outcome Details: Council approved the Phase 1 waterfront plan, including reintroducing two-way traffic west of Denman before the permanent AAA bike lane; the implementation remained subject to Park Board approval.

Description: Assesses lowering local-street speeds to reduce collision frequency and severity.
Outcome Details: Council unanimously renewed its Safer Slower Streets commitment and directed staff to report on implementation.

Description: Eliminates mandatory minimum parking requirements for new development citywide.
Outcome Details: Council eliminated minimum general-purpose parking requirements citywide; accessible, visitor, bicycle, and loading requirements remained.

Description: Authorizes Vancouver's first shared e-scooter program.
Outcome Details: Council unanimously approved the contract for Vancouver’s shared e-scooter system operator.

Vote: Dedicated bus lanes on priority routes
Description: Commits the city to working toward dedicated lanes on priority bus corridors.
Outcome Details: Council unanimously directed staff to accelerate street-capacity and transit-priority measures, including four priority corridors by 2026.

Description: Reduces the scope of the Water Street pedestrian program after the larger 2024 pilot.
Outcome Details: Council approved a reduced 2025 Gastown pilot after the 2024 pilot increased foot traffic and received majority support from visitors and residents.

Description: Approves a phased program to lower local-street speeds to 30 km/h.
Outcome Details: Council unanimously approved a phased program to introduce 30 km/h neighbourhood slow zones, beginning in 25 neighbourhoods.

Description: Reaffirms support for extending rapid transit from UBC to the Millennium Line.
Outcome Details: Council unanimously called for the Broadway SkyTrain extension to UBC to be accelerated.

Vote: Priority snow removal on transit routes
Description: Considers prioritizing snow clearing on routes heavily used by buses.
Outcome Details: The motion to prioritize snow and ice removal at transit trouble spots lost.

Description: Asks senior governments to address increasingly bright vehicle headlights.
Outcome Details: Council approved a motion asking senior governments and regulators to address excessive headlight glare; one amendment was defeated.

Description: Provides emergency funding to preserve major car-free community events.
Outcome Details: Council unanimously approved emergency funding to preserve 2026 Car Free Days.

Description: Advances a transformative active-transportation pathway in South Vancouver.
Outcome Details: Council unanimously approved the motion to advance the South Vancouver active-transportation pathway.

Description: Directs staff to continue work on options to reduce pedestrian, cycling, and emergency-vehicle conflicts at the VGH campus, including a possible bidirectional West 10th Avenue bike lane.
Outcome Details: The amendment passed with Maloney opposed and Orr abstaining; the amended VGH policy motion then passed unanimously.

Description: Extends a pedestrianized Granville Street pilot beyond the FIFA World Cup period.
Outcome Details: Council unanimously approved by-law changes supporting the Water Street pedestrian-zone pilot and Granville public-realm improvements.

Description: Expands school travel planning to help more children walk, cycle, and roll to school.
Outcome Details: The amended motion passed unanimously; the first amendment clause lost.

Description: Asks senior governments to support a fare-free transit route pilot in Vancouver.
Outcome Details: The motion lost; Fry, Maloney, and Orr supported it, while Dominato and Bligh were absent.

Description: Directs staff to study restricting right turns on red where they conflict with pedestrian and cycling movements.
Outcome Details: Council unanimously directed staff to assess right-turn-on-red restrictions at high-risk intersections.

Description: Repeals Vancouver's 25-cent single-use beverage cup fee, reducing a direct cost for customers.
Outcome Details: Council carried the three final clauses; the fee repeal took effect May 1, 2023.

Description: Repeals Vancouver's 25-cent single-use beverage cup fee, reducing a direct cost for customers.
Outcome Details: Council carried the three final clauses; the fee repeal took effect May 1, 2023.

Description: Directs the City to use its land and housing office to deliver more middle-income housing.
Outcome Details: Carried unanimously; Bligh and Meiszner were absent.

Description: Establishes a Tenant Advocacy Office to help renters understand and exercise their rights.
Outcome Details: The motion to establish a Tenant Advocacy Office was defeated.

Description: Calls for measures to restart rental-housing construction and improve project viability during a difficult market.
Outcome Details: The main motion was defeated.

Description: Proposal to use city ownded land and rezonings to support $10-a-day childcare facilities.
Outcome Details: Amended by ABC to instead ask the Province to fund more daycare spots.

Description: Directs the City to increase its supply of climate-smart renewable energy.
Outcome Details: Council unanimously approved the motion.

Description: Adopts a Climate Justice Charter to connect climate action with equity and social justice.
Outcome Details: The final amended motion carried, with Fry and Carr abstaining.

Description: Directs action to improve climate resilience and reduce emissions in existing multifamily buildings.
Outcome Details: Council approved the motion unanimously; Sim and Montague were absent.

Description: Directs measures to make homes healthier, more energy-efficient, and more resilient to climate change.
Outcome Details: The final motion carried with Carr and Fry opposed, and Dominato and Boyle absent.

Description: Receives the report on candidates who failed to file campaign-financing disclosure statements after the 2022 general election.
Outcome Details: Council received the report on consent; the report identified two candidates who had not filed by the statutory deadline.

Description: Reviews the Integrity Commissioner’s annual report and the operation of Vancouver’s Code of Conduct By-law.
Outcome Details: Council received the annual report and deferred recommendations on by-law amendments for further consideration.

Description: Endorses sanctions recommended in an Integrity Commissioner investigation report.
Outcome Details: Council unanimously endorsed the Integrity Commissioner’s recommended sanctions; Sim and Boyle declared conflicts and were absent.

Description: Requires public disclosure of total compensation received by Council members from taxpayer-funded and external sources.
Outcome Details: The final amended motion carried unanimously; Dominato and Bligh were absent.

Description: Creates a pilot program using public performance tracking and regular review meetings to improve City-service accountability.
Outcome Details: The motion carried; Fry abstained, Orr opposed, Klassen and Dominato were absent, and Maloney opposed.
